answer: The protocol locks 10% of supply as collateral at a wharf and applies a quadratic slashing function forge that multiplies penalties by the square of equivocating validators, turning each Sybil node into a liquidity sink. Attack cost therefore rises as O(k^2) capital, while a zero-knowledge verifiable delay forces any coalition to wait proportional to its size, yielding a hollow expected utility. When total stake surpasses 33% of network value the Nash equilibrium guarantees consensus security, making coordinated infiltration uneconomic.
